title: A dense-case theorem for Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture
summary: Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture asserts that every finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many exact second outneighbors as outneighbors. Established cases include tournaments, proved by Fisher (1996), and oriented graphs of minimum outdegree at most six, proved by Kaneko and Locke (2001); a recent preprint of Sadhukhan, Sandeep, and Sen (2026) treats minimum outdegree seven. For dense incomplete graphs, Fidler and Yuster (2007) proved the conjecture when the missing edges form a matching, a star, or a clique, Ghazal (2012) extended this direction to generalized stars,…
